business_scope.primary_industry_name: Maritime Seafarer Staffing and Vessel Crew Management Agency

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, as amended, and Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, ss 83.03, 462.31; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss 21.1-21.4 (register of individuals with significant control); An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss 2.4-2.7 (ultimate beneficiary declarations to the Registraire des entreprises); Regulation respecting the register of enterprise information, CQLR c P-44.1, r 1; Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1, ss 25 and 125; Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, ss 21 and 36.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent civil registry / passport authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the country of origin; Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Status of any foreign shareholder parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry of the foreign jurisdiction (e.g., Companies House, US Secretary of State)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency listing foreign directors and authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or registered agent of the foreign parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; notarized certification of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for service of process and incorporation nominee agent in Quebec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate grantor, executed before a notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn French translation of all constitutive documents and identity evidences
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: OQLF-recognized / OTTIAQ certified translator in Quebec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized attestation of translation conformity; no apostille required for domestic Quebec certification

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, UBOs, key employees, and crew candidates against: (a) Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2017, c 21; (b) United Nations Security Council consolidated list via the United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; (c) OFAC SDN List given USD wire settlement rails; (d) FINTRAC politically exposed persons criteria under PCMLTFA s 9.3 and FINTRAC Compliance Guidance; (e) Transport Canada verification of STCW certificates and MLC 2006 medical/fitness evidence for maritime personnel. Suspicious transactions must be filed with FINTRAC within 30 days under PCMLTFA s 7; large cash transaction reporting threshold is CAD 10,000; providing property or funds to listed terrorist entities is prohibited under Criminal Code s 83.03. The crewing agency will handle multi-currency payroll and family remittances, so registration as a Money Services Business (MSB) with FINTRAC must be assessed before activating foreign payroll services.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - online name reservation and constitution portal (https://www.registrairedesentreprises.gouv.qc.ca); federal alternative: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (https://www.ic.gc.ca) with NUANS Name Search report
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, s 21, and the Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1, s 25, the name of a Quebec business corporation must be in French unless exempted by recognized trademark status or established reputation under a non-French name; transliterated names are accepted only with a French distinctive or descriptive element. The name must contain a distinctive element, a descriptor (e.g., 'Gestion maritime' or 'Agence d'equipage'), and a legal element ('Inc.', 'Corp.', or 'Ltee').
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Commission (may falsely imply a government commission)
Municipal or municipal-district references implying official affiliation
Cooperative (unless actually constituted as a cooperative)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Quebec: if the Registraire refuses the proposed name, the applicant may, within 60 days, file a written request for administrative reconsideration with the Registraire des entreprises under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, submitting trademark evidence, transliteration rationale, or proof of established reputation; a further judicial review lies before the Superior Court of Quebec under the Code of Civil Procedure, CQLR c C-25.01, arts 529-548. Federal (CBCA): file a request for reconsideration with the Director of Corporations within 30 days of the refusal, then seek judicial review before the Federal Court under the Federal Courts Act, RSC 1985, c F-7, s 18. A rejected name may be re-filed with a new distinctive element and a fresh name search report.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. The corporate registered office under s 125 of the QBCA may be a professional registered-agent address acceptable to the Registraire. However, the CNESST labour placement agency licence under the Act respecting labour placement agencies and recruitment agencies of employees, CQLR c A-2.2, requires a fixed, identifiable establishment in Quebec where crew contracts, personnel files, and manning records are maintained. A pure virtual mail-drop address without a managed physical suite does not satisfy licence conditions once crew placement activities commence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate to elevated: approximately 45% likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection in the first operating year; the probability rises to 65-75% if MLC 2006 manning audits, Transport Canada STCW verification, or Temporary Foreign Worker Program compliance reviews are triggered. CNESST regularly inspects licensed placement and recruitment agencies for labour standards, record-keeping, and fee prohibition compliance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (CQLR c. S-31.1), ss. 9-16, 23-29, 101-114; supplemented by the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1), ss. 1-10.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec / Entreprises Québec, 800 Place d'Youville, Québec (Québec) G1R 3P4; online portal https://www.registraire.gouv.qc.ca/
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form D01-A — Articles of Incorporation (Articles constitutifs) under the Quebec Business Corporations Act, together with the initial declaration of registration (D02-A) filed with the Registraire des entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement under Quebec law. The articles may authorize shares with no par value. Capital may be called and paid in money or property value fixed by the directors. No escrow account required unless imposed by labour law or professional licensing obligations relevant to employment placement agencies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporator adopts this first board resolution to effect organization; the filed articles of incorporation are ratified. RESOLVED, that the shares of the corporation set forth in the Subscription List be accepted, allotted, and fully paid for by the subscribers, and that the Chief Financial Officer record subscriptions and issue certificates. RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at [address], Province of Québec, where the minute book and corporate records shall be kept. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Name] Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] Corporate Secretary, each authorized to execute documents and direct ordinary course business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Entreprises Québec online name request service / Registraire des entreprises du Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request at https://www.registraire.gouv.qc.ca/ and obtain a prioritized name search result (at least three proposed names). Keep the report; it is valid for 90 days and required for the articles. Verify absence of infringing trademarks and compliance with s. 30 QBCA.
required_dossiers: Description of business purpose (seafarer recruitment and crew management)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused or objected to, file a revised name report, provide consent from the holder, or rebut within 30 days; if refusal persists, apply to court under s. 31 QBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and notarized execution of articles of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary or barrister authorized in Québec; subsequent registry filing with Registraire des entreprises du Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft articles under s. 9 QBCA stating authorized share capital (unlimited common shares), transfer restrictions, directors' limits, and any special rights. The incorporator(s) must sign before a notary or witness; a declaration is included if incorporating by representative. Use Form D01-A prescribed by the Registraire.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a defect notice, amend the articles by filing a certificate of correction or refile within 30 days; fees are waived for first correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and registration; receipt of certificate of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Entreprises Québec) via online filing or in-person counters
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Form D01-A together with the declaration of registration under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; pay the required duties using accepted payment methods. Upon completion, the Registraire issues the Certificate of Registration (immatriculation) containing the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ). This is the forming moment under s. 28 QBCA.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If filing is delayed or queried, remedy by updating and resubmitting missing identification. If certification is refused, file an application for judicial remedy under s. 144 QBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of registered office, corporate records and minute book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors / corporate secretary; records address located in Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational board meeting. Adopt by-laws, approve share issuance to subscribers, receive payment of subscription price, and register the corporate seal. Maintain the minute book with articles, by-laws, resolutions, registers of directors and share transfers at the registered office. Provide notice of the registered address to the Registraire.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If corporate records are defective, call a ratification shareholders/board meeting. Failure to keep records is an offence but curable by supplementation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of directors/officers and filing of initial declaration (D02-A)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec; board resolution of authorized professional
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: At first board meeting, appoint CEO, CFO, and Secretary and have them sign consent/acceptance. File Form D02-A within 60 days of incorporation stating directors and officers' full names, addresses, and residential status. Also declare registered office and record the corporate activity codes including ISIC 5222 / NAICS 488390 where applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If late, pay the late receipt charge and file the declaration immediately; strike-off risk is averted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for CRA business number, GST/QST and payroll accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); Revenu Québec for QST and employer contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply through the CRA Business Registration Portal within 21 days of incorporation; obtain federal corporate income tax account and GST/HST account if supplies exceed $30,000. Register with Revenu Québec for QST, and if hiring employees, register for payroll source deductions and employer health services fund. For multi-currency crew payroll, instruct underwriters and payroll providers to record foreign currency payments in CAD equivalents.
required_dossiers: First board resolution opening bank accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA account is not activated within 30 days, call the Business Window and file the appropriate form; penalties are imposed for late registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Workplace health and safety registration and mandatory insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail); Revenu Québec for employer contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of hiring an employee, register as an employer with CNESST, obtain a workers' compensation financing attestation, and arrange liability insurance including professional indemnity for crew placement. Post a workplace notice. Determine classification code for employment agency operations and pay the required assessment.
required_dossiers: Insurance binder for commercial general liability
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CNESST sends a classification questionnaire, respond within 15 days and provide the classification of activity; failure to respond can lead to administrative penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for maritime crew recruitment agency permit and environmental compliance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère du Travail du Québec (licensing branch); Transport Canada (Marine Personnel); Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the private employment agency permit (permis d'agence de placement) under Quebec labour law and, if conducting seafarer placement, register with Transport Canada under the Maritime Labour Convention certification framework. For physical premises, obtain a fire safety certificate from the local fire service and a municipal occupancy permit. Complete an environmental self-assessment if vessel-shore transfer, waste storage, or fuel handling occurs.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licence is refused, request an administrative review or hearing before the Tribunal administratif du travail within 30 days; for environmental documentation, provide additional emissions calculations and apply for an attestation du MELCCFP.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère du Travail du Québec – Direction des licences d'agences de placement; Transport Canada – Marine Personnel Regulations; municipal building services
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permis d'agence de placement / Private Employment Agency Permit (Quebec) and Seafarer Recruitment and Placement Certificate (Maritime Labour Convention, 2006)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP), Québec
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exemption/Declaration – Registration under Schedule C if the activity is office-based crew recruitment without industrial wastewater discharge; classified as 'minimal' requiring simple registration and annual reporting. For waterfront crew transfer or vessel fuelling, a 'Full EIA Report' is required under the Environmental Quality Act, CQLR c. Q-2, ss. 31-31.1.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater from office activities; if crew amenities maintenance occurs, effluent must meet municipal sewer by-law BOD5 ≤ 300 mg/L, COD ≤ 700 mg/L, TSS ≤ 350 mg/L and pH 6.0–9.5; VOC emissions remain below 50 tonnes/year; oily water and bilge waste handled under Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate under Quebec's Building Act (Code de sécurité, c. B-1.1, r. 2) for occupancy under 200 persons; structural load inspections; emergency evacuation plan; occupational health and safety clearance from CNESST; first-aid kit and defibrillator if more than 25 employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html; Revenu Québec (Québec provincial tax authority) – revenuequebec.ca. Both administer corporate income tax, GST/HST, QST, payroll deductions, and related registration obligations for a Quebec-based corporation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-investor entity must (i) incorporate federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act or provincially under the Quebec Business Corporations Act, register with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, and obtain a Quebec establishment number; (ii) apply to CRA through Business Registration Online for a 9-digit Business Number (BN) with an RM account for corporate income tax; (iii) register for a GST/HST account if taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000; (iv) register for payroll deduction and source-withholding accounts with CRA if the agency employs seafarers or office staff in Canada; (v) register with Revenu Québec for QST, provincial corporate income tax, health-services-fund obligations, and Quebec payroll accounts; (vi) appoint an authorized representative in Canada and file the required Schedule 91 information for non-resident shareholding if applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – A Quebec-registered Canadian corporation is a taxable entity separate from its shareholders, resident in Canada, and subject to federal Part I tax plus Quebec provincial corporate tax on worldwide income. A branch of a foreign corporation is likewise taxed on Canadian-source business income at the entity level, with an additional federal Part XIV branch tax on after-tax profits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not use US-style check-the-box elections or hybrid-mismatch elections for entity classification; all corporations are automatic taxable entities. Available elective mechanisms include: Income Tax Act section 85 rollover election for tax-deferred transfers of qualifying property to a corporation; section 256 amalgamation and artificial-loss restriction elections; section 261 functional-currency reporting election for Canadian corporations; GST/HST group registration election under Excise Tax Act section 156; and the Quick Method election for smaller GST registrants. Revenu Québec allows corresponding elections under the Quebec Taxation Act where federal elections have a provincial equivalent.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax); Quebec uses separate federal GST and provincial QST rather than a single harmonized VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies made in Canada (GST/HST small-supplier threshold; QST threshold mirrors the GST threshold for Quebec). Most crew-recruitment agencies exceed this threshold immediately; voluntary registration is available below threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamp, or API-based fiscal stamping mandate exists under federal or Quebec indirect tax law. CRA accepts electronic invoices in auditable standard formats and requires mandatory electronic filing of GST/HST returns for most registered businesses. Revenu Québec permits electronic invoicing and mandates electronic B2B invoicing for suppliers to certain Quebec public-sector bodies through approved portals; ordinary B2B taxpayer invoices may be issued electronically if retained with complete audit trail.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A ship crew recruitment and vessel management agency may claim zero-rated GST/HST and QST treatment when it supplies a service to a non-resident customer (foreign shipowner or foreign manning agency) and the service is not an excepted supply, such as services in respect of Canadian real property, advisory/consulting services consumed in Canada, or services in respect of tangible personal property situated in Canada. Crewing services that support foreign-flag vessels engaged in international commercial voyages, where the foreign customer receives the benefit outside Canada, are generally zero-rated under Excise Tax Act Schedule VI, Part V (supplies to non-residents) and the parallel Quebec QST zero-rating provisions. The exporter must document the non-resident status of the customer, the offshore/international nature of the service, and contemporaneous evidence that the service is not used in Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Form B13A/B13B or Integrated Import Declaration) where crew stores, ship supplies, or goods are exported alongside crew services
Bill of Lading or Sea Waybill for any exported ship chandlery, equipment, or stores
Inward remittance certificate or Canadian bank FX credit advice / SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt of the foreign currency payment
Commercial invoice and signed crew management contract with the non-resident shipowner or manning principal
Seafarer employment contracts, crew list, MLC 2006 certificates, and evidence of embarkation on foreign-flag vessels
Proof of non-resident status of the customer, such as foreign ship registration documents or foreign corporate extract
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unsupported export zero-rating claims are treated as misstatements under the Excise Tax Act and the Quebec Taxation Act. CRA and Revenu Québec may deny the zero rate, reassess the supply as taxable GST/HST and QST, add arrears interest, and issue civil penalties under ETA sections 280 to 285, including penalties of 25% of the wrongly refunded or understated net tax and additional gross-negligence penalties under federal and provincial income tax rules. Knowingly making false export statements can lead to criminal prosecution under ETA section 327(1), fines up to twice the tax evaded, and imprisonment. The normal four-year reassessment period is extended to seven years where misrepresentation or negligence is established; retrospective clawbacks also trigger recovery of input tax credits previously claimed, with interest running from the original due date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) with the exchange-equivalent regulatory framework administered by OSFI (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions) and FINTRAC for cross-border transaction reporting
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full convertibility under IMF Article VIII. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely permitted, including dividend profit remittance and upstream loan repayments. Non-residents may repatriate funds without exchange-approval hurdles, subject to applicable withholding taxes under the Income Tax Act (notably Part XIII on dividends and non-resident service fees) and to documentary proof of source and compliance with the Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (FATCA) and the Canada-United States Enhanced Cross-Border Information Exchange.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory requirement exists to surrender export proceeds or any mandatory conversion ratio. Export receipts can be retained in a foreign currency at a Canadian chartered bank or an approved subsidiary account, because Canada operates a floating exchange-rate regime with inflation targeting. Reporting obligations are limited to OSFI anti-money-laundering thresholds (e.g., large cash and cross-border wire records), Statistics Canada International Transactions data surveys for transactions exceeding C$1 million per month, and any policy directive under the Special Economic Measures Act applicable to specific sanctioned counterparties.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate and constrained. Canada does not issue dedicated electronic-money-institution (EMI) licences. Non-bank payment platforms must register as money services businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. Offshore digital EMIs may assist in multi-currency crew payroll disbursement in a shadow-operations role, but they face severely limited viability for holding operational treasury because they cannot open a clearing account at the Bank of Canada nor hold insured Canadian deposit balances. The preferred architecture is a primary Canadian chartered bank account for corporate treasury with an MSB-licensed or OSFI-federally-regulated payroll-lite payment processor for crew card remittances.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: An in-person interview by a bank signatory or a designated branch compliance officer is normally expected for the initial directorship and primary signing authorities. Remote onboarding is legally permitted when the Canadian corporate registry record is verified through the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, when the directors are already known to the financial institution, or when the applicant engages a Canadian law firm that provides an accredited verification affidavit. Strategic foreign principals may be eligible for video-verified eKYC if the sending bank provides a notarized bank-to-bank letter of reference, certified passport copies, and proof of registered address; otherwise physical attendance at a Montréal, Toronto, or offshore RBC/TD private-banking office is required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: IMO/ISPS sanctions exposure — vessel owners, charterers, or ultimate beneficial owners are resident in or transacting from prohibited zones managed by Global Affairs Canada
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: KYC/KYB pack: seafarer employment agreements, vessel registry extract (IMO number and flag state), International Safety Management (ISM) certificate, charter party list, corporate chain with direct Global Affairs Canada compliance attestation, and a FINTRAC-compliant sanctions screening report generated by an OSFI-approved vendor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually high cash advance or ATM payout pattern for crew wages inconsistent with a 4,000-hour annual pre-pay fund
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-issued payroll ledger with full signatory approval chain, multi-currency disbursement schedule with exchange-rate snapshots, seafarer wage sign-offs under the Maritime Labour Convention (MLC 2006), and annual independent audit confirmation from the licensed crew recruitment agency showing no undisclosed wage advances.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unknown ultimate beneficial ownership or Québec civil-law trust complexities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Relevé d'entreprise (Registraire des entreprises du Québec), notarized trust deed, natural-person controlling declaration under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, and the FATCA / Canadian-Bank Confirmation and Self-Certification forms (CBCS) executed by all directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-currency remittance patterns that appear commercially unreasonable for seafarer jurisdictions with low payment probability
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Line-item statement of work under an international factoring and netting agreement, treasury-management module reconciliation, third-party ship-agency payroll processing report with audit trail, and a cleared sanctions screening record for the receiving crew list and payment fishing fleet.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant foreign shareholder equity or subordinated loan injection via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 into the Canadian bank settlement account. Use purpose codes consistent with Statistics Canada Direct Investment reporting (equity subscription code 'A990' or intercompany loan code 'A880') and attach an officer's confirmation of Part XIII if any interest/dividend component is paid out within a fiscally relevant period. Incoming settlement in CAD must first enter the dedicated Capital Escrow Account, then a journal entry transfers to the operational treasury account only after beneficial-owner verification and a sanctions check against Global Affairs Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for seafarer wage payments, supplier remittances, and operational transfers; (2) Commercial documentary letters of credit issued under UCP 600 for vessel-slip lease, ship-chandler supply, or large mobilization deposits; (3) Open-account T/T plus cross-border ACH for North-American and European suppliers. Settlements must be tagged to the beneficial beneficiary account with the Canadian routing transit number, a proper ISO 20022 structured remittance field, and an FINTRAC large-cross-border-wire return (reportable threshold) when the aggregate incident exceeds C$10,000. For every disbursement over C$25,000 the treasury operator should embed a two-person controls sign-off anchored in the KYC evidence and an internally auditable FX rate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable CAD/USD forward with a Canadian Schedule I bank
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) for currencies with settlement restrictions, executed only with an OSFI-regulated or swap-dealer counterparty
Cross-currency interest rate swap (CAD/USD) for matched operational-debt and seafarer-benefit liabilities
FX rollover swap (swap/forward points) for continuous multi-currency payroll flows
Cash-settled FX options (European-style) available through a Canadian investment dealer

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (Quebec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the enterprise's registration (e.g., registered March 15, due by May 14).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years may lead to an administrative dissolution notice from the REQ, and subsequent strike-off of the entity. No monetary late fee is assessed for a timely missed filing, but the risk of dissolution is the primary sanction.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (CBCA) – applicable only if the corporation is federally incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the anniversary of incorporation (e.g., incorporated March 15, due by May 14).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may trigger a notice of delinquency; continued non-filing for one year can lead to administrative dissolution by Corporations Canada after a final notice, and the corporate legal existence is dissolved.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue, asset, or size-based exemption under the QBCA; an auditor must be appointed unless the shareholders pass a unanimous resolution to dispense with the auditor. Public corporations and corporations governed by the CBCA are subject to mandatory audit requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) under the CPA Canada Handbook for private corporations; the chosen basis must be consistently applied.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec maintains a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (RISC) at the registered office. There is no separate annual UBO filing with the REQ, but the Annual Declaration requires an annual confirmation of directors and shareholders' data, including any changes to significant control. Share transfers must be recorded in the RISC within 15 days of the transaction, and the annual confirmation serves as a check of the RISC's accuracy. Access to the RISC is restricted to authorized government bodies and is not public.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book containing records of meetings and resolutions
Register of Individuals with Significant Control (RISC)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $110 - $370 USD per year (typical Quebec agent/registered office fees)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $2,200 - $7,400 USD per year (typical small private corporation audit fee in Quebec)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general corporate income tax rate: 15% federal and 11.5% Quebec. A qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation may generally access a combined small-business rate of approximately 12.2% on eligible active business income within the applicable annual business limit, subject to federal and Quebec eligibility, associated-corporation allocation, passive-income reduction, and other limitations.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal general rate reductions and the federal small-business deduction may reduce the federal rate to 9%. Quebec's small-business rate may reduce the Quebec rate to approximately 3.2% for qualifying corporations. The federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development regime, Quebec research and development incentives, accelerated capital cost allowance rules, and sector-specific refundable or non-refundable credits may apply only if statutory conditions are satisfied. A non-resident-controlled corporation generally cannot use the Canadian-controlled private corporation small-business deduction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, including applicable schedules, filed electronically through CRA-certified tax software or the Canada Revenue Agency Corporation Internet Filing service. A Quebec corporation or corporation carrying on business through a permanent establishment in Quebec generally files the Quebec CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return through Revenu Quebec's electronic filing system. GST/HST and Quebec QST returns are separate filings.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 and CO-17 are generally due within six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end. Any federal and Quebec corporate tax balance is generally due two months after year-end. A qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation may generally have a three-month balance-payment period if the statutory conditions are met; the return remains due within six months.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Business Number, corporation type, tax year start and end dates, address, province of permanent establishment, and whether the corporation is resident in Canada.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation must identify its Canadian permanent establishment, Canadian business activities, authorized representative, and applicable treaty position. A Canadian subsidiary is ordinarily a Canadian-resident corporation subject to Canadian filing on worldwide taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholder and corporate relationship information, including associated corporations, ownership, and control.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose non-resident parent ownership and associated-corporation relationships. Do not claim Canadian-controlled private corporation status unless all statutory control requirements are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting income or loss to income for tax purposes, including non-deductible expenses, taxable amounts, reserves, depreciation adjustments, and other permanent or temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude accounting expenses that are not incurred to earn income from a business or property in Canada. Apply Canadian thin-capitalization, interest-limitation, foreign-exchange, and withholding rules to cross-border amounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital cost allowance by class, additions, dispositions, undepreciated capital cost, and recapture or terminal loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only Canadian tax depreciation for eligible depreciable property used to earn Canadian income. Foreign vessel, office, software, and equipment costs require classification under Canadian capital-cost-allowance rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information concerning non-resident shareholders and shareholder ownership, where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report material non-resident ownership and changes. Maintain beneficial-ownership records supporting treaty eligibility and withholding-tax treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information relating to foreign income, foreign affiliates, foreign taxes, and foreign reporting obligations, where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Canadian corporation must examine foreign-affiliate, foreign-property, foreign-tax-credit, and treaty reporting obligations when it holds foreign accounts, investments, affiliates, or operational assets.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income statement by source, including revenue, payroll, commissions, subcontractor costs, operating expenses, and net income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separately track crewing-management fees, recruitment commissions, payroll administration charges, reimbursed crew expenses, related-party service fees, and pass-through amounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial statement information, accounting basis, and reporting entity details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use Canadian-dollar tax reporting and retain reconciliations from consolidated or foreign-parent accounting records to the Canadian legal entity's statutory accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital dividend account, refundable dividend tax, dividend refund, and related integration calculations, where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends to non-residents generally attract Part XIII withholding. Corporate tax integration accounts do not eliminate the obligation to withhold, remit, and report amounts paid to non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax payable, payments, installments, and information concerning non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File Form T106 where the statutory reporting conditions are met, including generally where reportable non-arm's-length non-resident transactions exceed the applicable aggregate threshold. Reconcile T106 values to the ledger, invoices, agreements, and transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Quebec CO-17 income and tax schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income, Quebec allocation, provincial deductions, credits, installments, and balance payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income to Quebec using applicable federal and Quebec allocation rules. A corporation with a Quebec establishment must file even where its head office is outside Quebec.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: RL-1, T4, T4A, NR4, and Revenu Quebec payroll information returns
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Employment income, commissions, fees, pension or other amounts, and non-resident payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Determine whether seafarers, recruiters, directors, and contractors are employees or independent contractors. Issue the correct slips and withhold income tax, CPP, QPP, EI, and QPIP where applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Federal corporate income tax late filing generally attracts 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% of unpaid tax for each complete month late, up to 12 months; increased penalties can apply after a formal demand to file. Interest accrues on unpaid tax, installments, and penalties at prescribed rates. Quebec imposes separate late-filing penalties and interest. Repeated failures, false statements, gross negligence, or intentional evasion can trigger additional penalties, reassessments, prosecution, and director liability.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid or credited by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident, subject to an applicable tax treaty or other statutory exemption. Common treaty rates may be 5% for qualifying corporate ownership and 15% for other dividends, but the applicable treaty and ownership conditions must be verified.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of residence or other acceptable documentary evidence from the beneficial owner, confirm treaty residence, beneficial ownership, limitation-on-benefits or anti-conduit conditions, ownership percentage, holding period, and entitlement to the reduced rate. Apply the reduced rate only where the payer has reasonable grounds to do so. File NR4 information returns and slips, remit tax generally by the 15th day of the month following payment, and retain Forms NR301, NR302, or NR303 where relevant. A Canadian payer remains liable for under-withholding, interest, and penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic Part XIII rate is generally 25% for royalties and other specified amounts paid to non-residents. Treaty rates commonly reduce qualifying copyright, patent, software, know-how, or other royalty payments to approximately 10%, but rates vary by treaty and royalty category. Arm's-length interest paid by a Canadian resident to a non-resident is generally exempt from Canadian withholding under domestic law, subject to exceptions including participating debt interest, certain related-party or non-arm's-length amounts, and other prescribed categories. Treaty rates and exemptions must be tested against the specific instrument, recipient, beneficial ownership, and related-party status.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canada generally does not prescribe a single monetary threshold that excuses contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation. A T106 information return is generally required for reportable non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents where the aggregate reportable amount exceeds CAD 1,000,000, subject to statutory exclusions and filing rules. The CAD 1,000,000 threshold is not a safe harbor from arm's-length pricing or documentation requirements. Canada has not adopted a standalone OECD-style mandatory Master File and Local File filing regime, but contemporaneous documentation must support material cross-border related-party transactions.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other reasonable methods supported by reliable evidence and consistent with Canadian transfer-pricing legislation and CRA administrative guidance
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no standalone general Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to the regimes in certain offshore jurisdictions. Substance remains relevant under the arm's-length principle, the general anti-avoidance rule, treaty anti-abuse principles, beneficial-ownership analysis, sham-transaction doctrine, corporate-residence rules, and characterization of services. A ship-crew recruitment agency should maintain Canadian personnel, decision-making, contracts, payroll, operational records, customer management, and risk control proportionate to the income claimed in Canada.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate tax evasion and false reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating crewing revenue, concealing recruitment commissions, fabricating expenses, maintaining undeclared offshore accounts, or knowingly submitting materially false T2 or CO-17 information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of tax, arrears interest, gross-negligence penalties generally equal to the greater of CAD 100 and 50% of the understated tax or overstated credits, civil tax-evasion penalties, and criminal prosecution. Criminal tax evasion can result in fines of up to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment of up to five years; aggravated cases can attract higher imprisonment exposure under the Income Tax Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face criminal prosecution, fines, imprisonment, director-liability assessments for unremitted source deductions, and civil recovery. A corporate form does not protect a director who personally participates in fraud or tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to remit payroll deductions and source withholdings
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to withhold or remit employee income tax, CPP, QPP, EI, QPIP, Part XIII tax, or amounts withheld from non-resident payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessments for the unremitted amount, prescribed interest, late-remittance penalties, repeated-failure penalties, and possible criminal prosecution. The payer may remain liable even if the amount was not collected from the recipient.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be jointly and severally liable for unremitted source deductions where statutory due-diligence defenses are unavailable. Criminal liability may arise for knowing non-remittance or obstruction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Excessive management fees, unsupported recruitment commissions, inflated royalty or interest charges, non-arm's-length payroll recharges, or shifting Canadian agency profit to a foreign related party without commercial evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment to arm's-length income, transfer-pricing penalty generally equal to 10% of the adjustment where the statutory conditions are met, interest, and possible reassessment beyond the normal period for misrepresentation or neglect.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil claims, derivative claims, shareholder claims, and personal exposure where they knowingly approve false records, fraudulent tax filings, or unlawful distributions. Ordinary pricing errors do not automatically create personal tax liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends, interest, or royalties through a conduit entity lacking beneficial ownership, misusing treaty residence certificates, or applying a reduced rate without verifying treaty entitlement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief, withholding-tax reassessment, interest, penalties, anti-avoidance adjustments, and possible application of the general anti-avoidance rule or treaty principal-purpose limitations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be liable for knowingly authorizing false withholding certificates or deliberate under-withholding. The payer corporation remains primarily liable for the tax shortfall.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends while insolvent, without adequate corporate authorization, or when the corporation cannot meet statutory solvency tests; disguising distributions as management fees or shareholder loans.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment or recovery of improper distributions, creditor remedies, tax reassessment, deemed-dividend treatment, interest, and penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize unlawful distributions may be jointly and severally liable to restore amounts, subject to statutory defenses. Fraudulent transfers can lead to civil remedies and criminal consequences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering, terrorist financing, or sanctions evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing unexplained crew-payroll wires, accepting funds from sanctioned vessel owners or intermediaries, structuring payments to avoid reporting, or failing to identify beneficial owners and suspicious transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties, compliance orders, criminal prosecution, forfeiture, asset freezes, and imprisonment. Proceeds-of-crime and terrorist-financing offenses can carry severe fines and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be prosecuted for authorization, acquiescence, wilful blindness, or obstruction. Corporate protection does not shield individuals who participate in money laundering or sanctions violations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed maritime recruitment or crewing activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a ship-crew recruitment or placement business without required federal, Quebec, maritime, employment-agency, immigration, privacy, or foreign-worker authorizations; charging prohibited recruitment fees to seafarers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative orders, license suspension or revocation, provincial and federal fines, repayment orders, immigration sanctions, contract invalidation, and criminal prosecution where applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may face regulatory prosecution, personal fines, civil claims by recruited workers, and imprisonment for knowing or reckless participation in unlawful placement, document fraud, trafficking, or exploitation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Treating employees or seafarers as independent contractors to avoid payroll tax, CPP/QPP, EI, QPIP, workers' compensation, vacation pay, or employment-standard obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive payroll assessments, source deductions, employer contributions, interest, penalties, wage orders, administrative penalties, and audits by federal or Quebec authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for certain unpaid wages, source deductions, and statutory remittances. Intentional misclassification can also support fraud or tax-evasion proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to retain contracts, crew payroll records, invoices, transfer-pricing analyses, shareholder registers, beneficial-ownership records, or evidence supporting tax residence and treaty claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure-to-file or failure-to-provide-information penalties, denial of deductions or treaty relief, reassessment based on available information, audit extensions, and prosecution for obstruction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face compliance orders, contempt or obstruction consequences, and personal exposure where records were deliberately destroyed, falsified, or withheld.
